executive_summary: Scattered Spider has reconstituted following 2024 arrests and is actively targeting UK retail with DragonForce ransomware, claiming two major victims — Marks & Spencer and Co-op UK — in a single week through helpdesk vishing and SIM-swapping to bypass identity controls.

Adversary-in-the-Middle phishing kits including Evilginx2 and Tycoon 2FA are stealing Microsoft Entra ID session tokens post-MFA at scale, rendering standard TOTP and SMS authentication ineffective against a now-commoditized attack technique.

CISA added four CVEs to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog this week — Commvault Command Center (CVSS 10.0 pre-auth RCE), SonicWall SMA100 (auth bypass), Windows CLFS (ransomware-exploited LPE), and Qualitia Active! Mail — all with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.

Russian SVR-linked APT29 has launched a new spearphishing wave against European diplomatic staff using GRAPELOADER and WINELOADER malware staged through convincing Ministry of Foreign Affairs wine-tasting event lures, representing a stealth-optimized evolution of existing TTPs.

Play ransomware operators exploited a Windows Common Log File System zero-day (CVE-2025-29824) for privilege escalation in attacks against small-to-medium businesses and critical infrastructure before Microsoft patched it on April 2025 Patch Tuesday.

cyber_news.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing Kits Bypassing MFA — Microsoft Entra ID Session Tokens Hijacked at Scale
cyber_news.summary: Multiple threat actors are deploying Evilginx2, Tycoon 2FA, and Modlishka AiTM reverse-proxy frameworks to intercept Microsoft Entra ID session tokens immediately after a legitimate MFA challenge completes. Microsoft Threat Intelligence has confirmed a significant escalation in campaigns targeting M365 tenants across industries. The attack renders standard TOTP authenticator apps and SMS-based MFA ineffective, as the attacker captures the authenticated session cookie rather than the credential itself.
cyber_news.expanded: The attack chain works by positioning the AiTM proxy between the victim and the legitimate Microsoft authentication endpoint — the victim completes MFA normally against the real IdP, but the proxy relays and captures the resulting session cookie in real time. Evilginx2 and Tycoon 2FA are sold as crimeware-as-a-service with low per-campaign costs, making this technique broadly accessible beyond sophisticated APT groups. The hijacked session token is then replayed from an attacker-controlled IP or residential proxy, appearing in Entra ID sign-in logs as an 'unfamiliar sign-in properties' event rather than a failed authentication — a subtle signal that many tenants miss. Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) can revoke compromised tokens in near-real-time when IP or session anomalies are detected, but it must be explicitly configured; FIDO2/passkey-based authentication defeats AiTM structurally because the cryptographic binding is domain-specific and cannot be proxied.

cyber_news.title: Scattered Spider / UNC3944 Reactivates with DragonForce RaaS — UK Retail Sector in Crosshairs
cyber_news.summary: Despite five member arrests in 2024, the English-speaking social-engineering collective Scattered Spider has reconstituted and is operating with a new ransomware-as-a-service partnership under the DragonForce brand. The group has claimed two major UK retail victims this week — Marks & Spencer and Co-op UK — with M&S suffering confirmed operational disruption estimated at over £300 million in impact. Scattered Spider continues to rely on helpdesk vishing and SIM-swapping as primary identity bypass mechanisms rather than technical exploits.
cyber_news.expanded: Scattered Spider's operational model is notable for its almost exclusive reliance on social engineering at the identity layer rather than vulnerability exploitation — attackers impersonate employees or IT contractors in calls to helpdesks and mobile carriers, convincing operators to reset MFA devices or port phone numbers. With DragonForce providing the encryption payload and data-leak extortion infrastructure, Scattered Spider functions effectively as an initial access and lateral movement specialist within a RaaS supply chain. The M&S incident reportedly involved compromise of the Active Directory environment and deployment of ransomware to virtualization infrastructure, causing prolonged disruption to contactless payment and online ordering systems. The group's reconstitution after the 2024 arrests suggests either core members avoiding prosecution retained operational knowledge, or knowledge transfer occurred to a successor generation within the same online communities.

cyber_news.title: APT29 / Midnight Blizzard Targets European Diplomats via Fake Wine-Tasting Event Invitations
cyber_news.summary: Russia's SVR-linked APT29, tracked by Microsoft as Midnight Blizzard, has launched a targeted spearphishing campaign against European diplomatic staff using lures impersonating official Ministry of Foreign Affairs event invitations, specifically wine-tasting receptions. The campaign delivers two malware families — GRAPELOADER, a stealthy initial-stage loader, and the previously documented WINELOADER backdoor — with the themed lures designed to appear credible to diplomatic targets. The campaign represents a tactical evolution of APT29's existing tooling toward more modular, staged delivery.
cyber_news.expanded: GRAPELOADER functions as a first-stage implant responsible for profiling the victim environment and selectively deploying WINELOADER only on validated high-value targets, reducing exposure of the more capable backdoor to security researcher sandboxes. The loader uses DLL side-loading techniques and in-memory execution to minimize filesystem artifacts, reflecting APT29's documented emphasis on operational security and long-term persistence in sensitive government networks. WINELOADER itself communicates over encrypted HTTPS with C2 infrastructure using legitimate-appearing cloud provider ASNs, making network-layer detection challenging without SSL inspection. The wine-tasting social engineering theme exploits the genuine prevalence of such diplomatic reception invitations among EU foreign ministry staff, lending the phishing emails a high degree of contextual plausibility.

cyber_news.title: Play Ransomware Exploited Windows CLFS Zero-Day (CVE-2025-29824) for Privilege Escalation Before Patch
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft confirmed that Play ransomware operators leveraged CVE-2025-29824, a zero-day vulnerability in the Windows Common Log File System driver, to escalate privileges to SYSTEM in attacks against SMBs and critical infrastructure in North America and Europe prior to the April 2025 Patch Tuesday release. The vulnerability has since been added to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Affected Windows versions include Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server 2016 through 2022.
cyber_news.expanded: CVE-2025-29824 is a use-after-free vulnerability in clfs.sys, the kernel driver underpinning the Windows Common Log File System — a component present across virtually all modern Windows installations and frequently overlooked in prioritization given its low profile. Play ransomware exploited the flaw as a local privilege escalation primitive after achieving initial access through other means, enabling the operator to move from a low-privileged foothold to SYSTEM-level control necessary for disabling security tooling and deploying ransomware payloads across the network. The CLFS subsystem has been a recurring source of Windows LPE vulnerabilities — CVE-2022-24521 and CVE-2023-28252 were similarly exploited by ransomware operators in prior years — suggesting threat actors systematically research and stockpile exploits for this driver. Play is a double-extortion ransomware group that has been active since 2022, targeting mid-market organizations with a pattern of rapid lateral movement following initial access.

cyber_news.title: Commvault CVE-2025-34028 Actively Exploited — CVSS 10.0 Pre-Auth RCE via File Upload
cyber_news.summary: A critical pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability in Commvault Command Center (CVE-2025-34028, CVSS 10.0) is being actively exploited in the wild, prompting an emergency CISA KEV addition with a federal patch deadline of three weeks. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary files to the Commvault server and achieve full system compromise without any credentials. On-premises Commvault deployments used for enterprise backup management are directly at risk.
cyber_news.expanded: The vulnerability resides in the file upload handling logic of the Commvault Command Center web interface, which fails to enforce authentication before processing file write operations — a pre-authentication attack surface that grants attackers an immediate foothold without any prior credential access. Exploitation leads directly to arbitrary code execution under the Commvault service account, which in backup environments typically holds privileged access to large portions of the enterprise infrastructure including databases, file servers, and endpoint backup agents. Backup infrastructure is a high-value target for ransomware operators specifically because compromising it simultaneously enables data exfiltration and destroys the victim's ability to recover without paying ransom. No viable workaround has been confirmed; vendor guidance requires immediate patching to remediated versions.

cyber_news.title: SonicWall SMA100 CVE-2025-32819 Zero-Day Exploited — Unauthenticated Admin Credential Reset
cyber_news.summary: A critical authentication bypass and path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2025-32819, CVSS 9.8) in SonicWall SMA100 series SSL-VPN appliances is being actively exploited, enabling unauthenticated remote attackers to reset administrator credentials and achieve full device compromise. Affected models include SMA 200, 210, 400, 410, and 500v. CISA has added the CVE to the KEV catalog and patches are available.
cyber_news.expanded: The vulnerability combines an authentication bypass with a path traversal flaw, allowing a remote attacker with no prior credentials to reach administrative API endpoints that should be protected. Successful exploitation permits the attacker to overwrite the admin password hash in the device configuration, granting full management control — including the ability to modify VPN split-tunneling rules, extract VPN client credentials, pivot into the protected network, or deploy persistent backdoors on the appliance firmware. SonicWall SMA100 appliances are pervasive in SMB and mid-market environments, frequently deployed by MSPs as the primary remote access gateway for client networks, making successful exploitation a direct path into managed client infrastructure. This device family has been repeatedly targeted by sophisticated threat actors including CISA-attributed nation-state groups since 2021, and known exploit code for prior SonicWall vulnerabilities is widely available in underground markets.

cyber_news.title: Fake IT Support Domains and SEO Poisoning Delivering RATs to MSP Client Searches
cyber_news.summary: Threat actors are systematically SEO-poisoning search results for common MSP and RMM tools — including ConnectWise, AnyDesk, and generic remote support software queries — to serve AsyncRAT and Lumma Stealer payloads via convincing lookalike download pages. Cisco Talos identified clustered infrastructure impersonating legitimate IT support brands, with victims primarily being SMB end users who independently search for remote access software. The campaign is particularly dangerous in MSP-managed environments where users may be expecting to install remote support tools.
cyber_news.expanded: The attacker infrastructure identified by Talos uses typosquatted domains combined with black-hat SEO techniques including link farms, keyword stuffing, and abuse of legitimate high-authority domains to push malicious pages into top search results positions — sometimes above the legitimate vendor's own listing. The fake download pages serve trojanized installers that bundle the legitimate application with an AsyncRAT or Lumma Stealer payload, executing the malware silently during what appears to be a normal software installation. AsyncRAT provides the attacker with persistent remote access, keylogging, and screen capture capabilities; Lumma Stealer harvests browser-saved credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and session cookies before exfiltrating to C2. The confluence of MSP tool impersonation with info-stealer delivery is particularly dangerous because stolen credentials from a technician's workstation can yield access to RMM platforms controlling hundreds of downstream client environments.

cyber_news.title: Microsoft DCU and Law Enforcement Seize 2,300+ Lumma Stealer C2 Domains — Variants Already Rebuilding
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit, in coordination with Europol and the U.S. Department of Justice, executed a major takedown operation seizing over 2,300 Lumma Stealer command-and-control domains. Lumma is one of the most widely distributed information-stealing malware families, delivered primarily through malvertising and cracked-software distribution networks. Security researchers are already observing affiliate operators rapidly rebuilding replacement infrastructure, limiting the long-term impact of the disruption.
cyber_news.expanded: Lumma Stealer operates as a malware-as-a-service platform sold on Russian-language cybercriminal forums, with a tiered subscription model that allows low-sophistication actors to deploy purpose-built credential harvesting campaigns with minimal technical knowledge. The malware targets browser-stored credentials, saved passwords, session cookies, cryptocurrency wallets, and two-factor authentication application databases — providing attackers with immediate access to a wide range of accounts following a single endpoint compromise. The DCU's domain seizure disrupts existing C2 communications for currently deployed implants, but the MaaS model means the underlying developer and affiliate network remain operational; historical precedent from similar takedowns (Emotet, Qakbot) indicates infrastructure reconstitution within days to weeks. The timing of the takedown coincides with elevated Lumma distribution via SEO-poisoning campaigns targeting MSP tool searches, described separately in this briefing.

cyber_news.title: North Korean IT Worker Scheme Expands to European Firms Using AI-Generated Deepfake Personas
cyber_news.summary: DPRK-linked operatives are expanding their fraudulent remote IT worker placement program beyond U.S. targets into European companies, now using AI-generated deepfake video profiles and synthetic identity documents to pass hiring screenings. CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Unit 42 both published updated research this week documenting the expanded targeting scope. Operatives primarily seek developer and cloud administrator roles to exfiltrate intellectual property and generate revenue for North Korea's weapons programs.
cyber_news.expanded: The scheme involves networks of DPRK-controlled operatives — sometimes called 'IT warriors' — who apply for remote technical positions using fabricated identities supported by AI-generated profile photos, deepfake video interview capabilities, and fraudulent work history documentation. Once placed, operatives pursue privileged access to source code repositories, cloud infrastructure, and internal systems, with exfiltrated intellectual property sold or transferred to state programs. Unit 42 researchers note that operatives frequently request camera-off accommodations during video calls or use real-time face-swap technology when cameras are required, and login activity commonly originates from VPN exit nodes inconsistent with the stated work location. The expansion to European targets reflects both increased scrutiny of the scheme in the U.S. and the comparatively less mature threat awareness among European HR and security teams regarding DPRK insider threat activity.

cyber_news.title: New 'ToyMaker' Initial Access Broker Sells Critical Infrastructure Footholds to Cactus Ransomware
cyber_news.summary: Cisco Talos published research identifying a new financially motivated initial access broker dubbed ToyMaker, which specializes in compromising healthcare, energy, and manufacturing organizations and selling established network footholds to ransomware operators including Cactus. ToyMaker deploys a custom backdoor called LAGTOY following exploitation of externally exposed services, establishing persistent access that is subsequently monetized through sale to ransomware affiliates. The IAB model separates initial compromise from ransomware deployment, complicating attribution and incident response.
cyber_news.expanded: LAGTOY is a lightweight custom backdoor that provides ToyMaker with persistent shell access while maintaining a minimal footprint to avoid detection during the dwell period between initial compromise and access sale. The multi-stage model — exploitation by ToyMaker, dwell and reconnaissance, then handoff to Cactus ransomware operators for monetization — means victims may experience a substantial gap between initial compromise and any detectable ransomware activity, during which the attackers conduct extensive network mapping and data staging. ToyMaker's focus on external-facing service exploitation as an entry vector aligns with the widespread exposure of legacy VPN appliances, unpatched RDP endpoints, and internet-facing management interfaces common in operational technology environments serving healthcare and energy sectors. Cactus ransomware, which received the access, is known for double-extortion and has specifically targeted organizations with significant OT/IT convergence.

cyber_news.title: CISA and NSA Release Updated Identity and Access Management Best Practices for Cloud-Era Environments
cyber_news.summary: CISA and NSA jointly released an updated Identity and Access Management advisory that supersedes the 2023 version, incorporating guidance for cloud-first and hybrid identity architectures, mandating phishing-resistant MFA for privileged accounts, and introducing recommendations for Privileged Identity Workstations. The guidance is directly applicable to MSP client environments operating hybrid Microsoft Entra ID and on-premises Active Directory configurations. The publication arrives in the same week as multiple AiTM MFA-bypass incidents and social-engineering attacks targeting identity controls.
cyber_news.expanded: The updated guidance introduces the concept of the Privileged Identity Workstation — a hardened, dedicated endpoint used exclusively for administrative tasks — as a foundational control for organizations managing privileged cloud identities, reflecting the reality that credential theft via compromised admin workstations is a primary enterprise attack vector. The advisory explicitly classifies TOTP-based authenticator apps and SMS as insufficient for privileged account MFA given the demonstrated effectiveness of AiTM proxy attacks, and mandates FIDO2 or certificate-based authentication for administrator roles. New cloud-specific guidance addresses Entra ID Conditional Access policy baselines, service principal credential hygiene, and workload identity federation as areas where organizations commonly maintain exploitable gaps. The joint CISA/NSA imprimatur gives MSPs a high-authority reference document to support client conversations about MFA upgrade investments.

cyber_news.title: OPSEC Failure Exposes Chinese Salt Typhoon Tooling Details in Ongoing Telecom Intrusions
cyber_news.summary: New research from Palo Alto Unit 42 and CrowdStrike reveals additional technical details about Salt Typhoon's tooling and techniques following an operational security failure by the threat actor group, which has been conducting persistent intrusions against telecommunications providers and ISPs. The group employs a sophisticated living-off-the-land approach targeting Cisco and Juniper network infrastructure using legitimate management protocols and built-in device capabilities to avoid detection. Congress received a classified briefing on the campaign's scope according to CyberScoop.
cyber_news.expanded: Salt Typhoon's documented approach involves deep exploitation of network operating systems — particularly IOS XE and Junos — using legitimately provisioned management access obtained through credential theft or exploitation of management-plane vulnerabilities, then leveraging native features such as GRE tunneling, policy-based routing, and embedded scripting to maintain persistence and conduct traffic interception without deploying traditional malware. The OPSEC failure that exposed additional tooling details reportedly involved attacker-controlled infrastructure being linked to known Salt Typhoon C2 clusters through misconfigured operational infrastructure, enabling researchers to enumerate additional campaign targets and techniques. The campaign's focus on ISP and telecom infrastructure gives the group the ability to intercept unencrypted communications and conduct targeted surveillance at a network level above individual endpoints — a capability with significant implications for any organizations whose traffic transits compromised carrier infrastructure.

deep_dive.title: Adversary-in-the-Middle Phishing Kits Bypassing MFA — Microsoft Entra ID Session Token Theft Escalating
deep_dive.content: The escalating adoption of Adversary-in-the-Middle phishing frameworks represents a fundamental shift in the threat model for Microsoft 365 environments and directly undermines the MFA deployments that most organizations have treated as their primary identity security control. The attack architecture is deceptively simple but highly effective: tools like Evilginx2, Tycoon 2FA, and Modlishka operate as transparent reverse proxies positioned between the victim and Microsoft's legitimate authentication infrastructure. The victim is directed to the proxy via a phishing link, completes the entire authentication flow — including MFA challenge — against the real Microsoft IdP relayed through the proxy, and receives what appears to be a successful login. Simultaneously, the proxy captures the authenticated session cookie issued by Microsoft after MFA completion. This cookie is then replayed by the attacker from a separate IP address, granting full access to the M365 tenant with no further authentication required. Critically, from Microsoft's logging perspective, both the legitimate victim session and the attacker's replayed session appear as 'successful' authentications — the attack leaves no failed login events. Detection relies on identifying the attacker's token replay as an anomalous sign-in, surfaced in Entra ID as 'unfamiliar sign-in properties' — a medium-severity alert that is frequently suppressed or deprioritized in high-volume environments. Evilginx2 and Tycoon 2FA are commercially available as crimeware-as-a-service, with phishing kit infrastructure available to low-sophistication actors for as little as a few hundred dollars per campaign, meaning this technique is no longer the exclusive domain of sophisticated APT groups. Microsoft's Continuous Access Evaluation framework offers meaningful mitigation by enabling near-real-time token revocation when IP address anomalies or other policy violations are detected, but CAE must be explicitly enabled per tenant and requires compatible client applications. The only architectural defense that defeats AiTM by design is FIDO2/passkey authentication: the cryptographic attestation is domain-bound and cannot be proxied, meaning the attacker's infrastructure — operating on a different domain — cannot obtain a valid credential even if it successfully relays the authentication attempt. For privileged accounts and IT administrators managing M365 tenants, FIDO2 hardware keys represent the minimum acceptable MFA standard given the current threat landscape.

biggest_hacks.title: Marks & Spencer Cyberattack — Scattered Spider / DragonForce Ransomware Confirmed, Operations Disrupted
biggest_hacks.summary: UK retail giant M&S suffered a confirmed Scattered Spider / DragonForce ransomware attack causing sustained disruption to contactless payments and online ordering, with estimated financial impact exceeding £300 million and representing the first publicly confirmed post-arrest Scattered Spider operation.

biggest_hacks.title: Co-op UK Confirms Cyberattack with Data Exfiltration — Scattered Spider TTPs Identified
biggest_hacks.summary: UK Co-operative Group confirmed a cyberattack resulting in exfiltration of member and employee data after initially downplaying the incident, with investigators linking the TTPs to the same Scattered Spider cluster responsible for the concurrent M&S attack.

biggest_hacks.title: PowerSchool Extortion Escalates — Individual School Districts Receive Direct Ransom Demands
biggest_hacks.summary: Attackers behind the late-2024 PowerSchool breach are now directly extorting individual school districts with ransom demands despite PowerSchool having previously paid a ransom for data deletion, exposing student PII, staff SSNs, and special education records across North American districts.

biggest_hacks.title: Ascension Health Discloses Additional Patient Data Exposure via Third-Party Vendor Breach
biggest_hacks.summary: Healthcare giant Ascension filed a supplementary breach notification disclosing additional patient record exposure linked to a downstream vendor compromise, compounding the regulatory and litigation exposure from the organization's 2024 ransomware incident.

biggest_hacks.title: Nova Scotia Power / Emera Cyberattack — Customer Billing Data Stolen, Grid Operations Isolated
biggest_hacks.summary: Canadian utility Nova Scotia Power confirmed attackers accessed customer billing data and personal information, with the company reporting that critical OT and grid operations systems were successfully isolated, and regulatory filings initiated for what may be a ransomware precursor or data-theft-only extortion event.

vulnerabilities.description: Pre-authentication arbitrary file upload vulnerability enabling full remote code execution on Commvault Command Center without any credentials. Actively exploited in the wild; CISA KEV listed with federal patch deadline. Backup infrastructure compromise gives attackers access to broad enterprise systems and destroys recovery options. Patch immediately — no sufficient workaround exists.

Authentication bypass combined with path traversal in SonicWall SMA100 SSL-VPN appliances, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to reset administrator credentials and achieve full device compromise. Actively exploited in the wild; CISA KEV listed. Pervasive in MSP-managed edge environments as primary remote access gateway. Patch immediately and audit for signs of prior compromise.

Stack-based buffer overflow in Qualitia Active! Mail 6 email client enabling unauthenticated remote code execution. Actively exploited; CISA KEV listed. Primarily affects Japanese organizations. Low prevalence in Western MSP environments but patch if present.

vulnerabilities.product: Windows Common Log File System (CLFS) Driver — Windows 10/11, Server 2016–2022
vulnerabilities.description: Use-after-free local privilege escalation zero-day in the Windows CLFS kernel driver, exploited by Play ransomware operators to escalate from low-privileged access to SYSTEM prior to April 2025 Patch Tuesday release. CISA KEV listed. Affects virtually all modern Windows versions. Confirm April 2025 Cumulative Update is deployed across all Windows endpoints and servers — prioritize Server 2016/2019.
